RUN-009.notes: Recovery, generation fencing and effect reconciliation. crates/server/src/runtime/recovery rebuilds a run's position from durable state only: plan.rs holds the pure decisions (the safe action for a durable position, and the generation fence) and service.rs applies them over the canonical stores. The precedence is the runtime's: honour a cancellation requested before the crash, reconcile an uncertain effect before any further work, stay parked on a wait the run itself owns, and only then resume. Fencing mirrors the runtime's own rule (`Generation::accept`): an actor behind the run's generation is stale and its output is discarded, while a newer generation supersedes the run's — refusing a newer generation would refuse recovery itself, which is why the earlier stricter rule was corrected. Reconciliation is applied from evidence (`ReconciliationEvidence::Determined` when the class has a deterministic check, `Manual` otherwise) and never by dispatching again; a `run.stale_worker_fenced` event records discarded work. `RECOVERY_READ_TABLES` declares the complete read set (runs, turns, steps, attempts, protocol_states via the store, runtime_events, checkpoints, effect_records, evidence, work_nodes) and a structural test scans the module's SQL literals and fails if any other table is referenced — memory tables above all — so 'recovery is not memory' is enforced, not merely intended.
